rules.title: Security Deposit Law – maximum security deposit
rules.requirement: A landlord may not collect a security deposit of more than one and one-half times one month's rent. Any additional yearly increase may not exceed 10% of the current deposit, and a pet deposit combined with the regular deposit may not exceed one and one-half times one month's rent.
rules.key_value: one and one-half times one month's rent; yearly increase not to exceed 10% of the current security deposit
rules.coverage_text: Most residential rental properties, including mobile homes. Landlords are not required to collect a deposit, but if they do they must follow the rules.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, unless the tenant makes the law applicable 30 days after sending a written request to the landlord.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ).

rules.title: No eviction merely because lease term ended
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot evict a tenant just because the lease term has ended. The only reason a landlord can terminate a lease is if they offer a new lease with different terms and the tenant does not agree.
rules.coverage_text: Residential tenants in New Jersey, as described in the publication's lease termination section.
rules.citation: NJ DCA Truth in Renting publication, Termination of a Lease Agreement
rules.quoted_span: A landlord cannot evict a tenant just because the lease term has ended.
